transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Um, hi. Yeah... I guess I'm just here because my mind won't really stop. It's just constantly jumping around. 

Like... worrying if our lab's new partnership is going to cut my position. Or, I don't know, if my data is wrong. And then it's... bills piling up, or my family thinking I'm falling behind. Just... stuff like that. And whether I've already ruined my chances at grad school. 

So... yeah. That's mostly it.
Do you find that these worries come up even when there isn’t a specific stressor or problem happening at the moment?

I mean... I don't really know. It's hard to tell. It just sort of feels like there's always something to think about, so... I haven't really noticed if it happens when nothing is going on. I don't really keep track of it like that.
Do you feel like your worrying is something you can’t really control, even when you try to stop thinking about these things?

Yeah... I guess. I mean, I try to. I'll tell myself to just focus on one task... like finishing a report, or checking an assay at the lab. But... it doesn't really work. One thing just sets off another. And then... I don't know, pretty soon I'm just staring at the screen, and my head is just running through every possible way things could go wrong. So... no. I can't really stop it.
Have you noticed any physical symptoms, like restlessness, trouble sleeping, muscle tension, or feeling easily fatigued, that seem to go along with all this worrying?

Um... yeah, I guess so. I don't know, it's just... I can't really sit still. Like at work, I feel pretty wound up. I can't just settle into my chair and focus. 

I end up... tapping my foot a lot. Or I'll keep checking my messages. Sometimes I just... walk back to the instrument room even if I don't need to. And... I don't know, if someone drops something or there's just a normal noise in the lab, I jump. It just... startles me. So, yeah. I guess I get restless.
Do you find yourself worrying about a variety of different things, not just one specific issue, and does it feel like you're always anticipating disaster in different areas of your life?

Yeah... I guess. It's... it's not just one thing. My mind kind of just... jumps around a lot. 

Like... I'll start thinking about work, and if this new partnership at the lab is going to cut my position. Or... if my data is wrong. And then... I don't know, it just shifts to other stuff. Like my bills piling up... or my family. I keep thinking they assume I'm falling behind. And... whether I've already ruined my chances at grad school. 

So... yeah. I guess I do expect things to go wrong... everywhere.
Do you notice these symptoms even when there isn’t anything specific causing you stress or worry at that moment?

Um... I don't really know. It's hard to tell. It feels like there's always... something going on. So I'm not sure if there's ever a time when nothing is stressing me out. I haven't really paid attention to that.
Do these worries and the way you’re feeling interfere with your ability to do your job, be productive, or function the way you’d like in your daily life?

Um... yeah, I guess it does. 

I... I missed a deadline at the lab recently. It was just an internal thing, but... I couldn't get my writing organized, or review the data properly. It was just... too much. 

And, I don't know, even normal stuff is hard right now. Like putting together routine reports. Or... going to art nights. Even just cooking for my family. It all just... feels like too much to keep up with.
How long have you been experiencing these worries and physical symptoms? Has it been going on for at least six months?

Um... yeah. It's been a while. 

I guess... about seven months? That's when the lab's funding shifted... and we got this new commercial partnership. It just... changed how everything was run. So... yeah, since then.
Have you noticed yourself feeling down, hopeless, or losing interest in things you usually enjoy, like your art nights or spending time with family?

Um... I don't think so. I mean, I still care about those things. I just... I'm just tired, I guess. It's not that I don't want to do them, it's just... hard to find the energy right now. But I don't feel hopeless or anything. Just... overwhelmed.
Have you found that things you used to enjoy, like your art or time with family, don't interest you as much anymore?
I... I think I just said this. I still care about them. I'm just... tired.
Do you find that you feel excessive anxiety and worry more days than not?

Yeah... I guess so. Most days. That's... kind of why I came in. 

My mind just... it's constantly jumping around. It doesn't really stop. I'll be worrying about whether the lab's new partnership is going to cut my position... and then it shifts to whether my data is wrong. And then it's just... bills piling up, or... worrying that my family thinks I'm falling behind. Or that I've already ruined my chances at grad school. It's just... always something.
Do you find it hard to concentrate because your mind is so full of worries?
Yeah... I guess so. Sometimes I'll be trying to read a paper for work, and I just... I have to read the same paragraph over and over. My brain is just somewhere else.
